role: external oracle for the electric near field inside a layer of axis-aligned rectangular walls: 3D finite-element fields of a metal block, a square hole in a metal film, a dielectric square and a metal rectangle, which the solve in stretched coordinates (Numerics.wall_resolution) and the unstretched solve are measured against

references.build: FEniCS (dolfin) 2019.1.0 underneath, gmsh 4.15.2 for the geometry and the mesh, MUMPS direct solve out of core; Python 3.14.10, from conda-forge

modified.description: used through its public Python API; the package itself was not changed

references.settings: Maxwell3DPeriodic on one eighth of the cell, using the exact mirror symmetries of normal incidence with E along x (the x mirror a perfect electric wall, the y mirror a perfect magnetic wall, and an even/odd split in z, two solves); second-order edge (Nedelec) elements; a perfectly matched layer above. Two scripts of the same construction. E_metal_block and E_hole: the block model, direct solves with block low-rank compression at 1e-9, relative residuals 1.1e-5 and 1.1e-5 (block), 4.0e-6 and 2.6e-6 (hole); R = 0.356150 and T = 0.611546 (block), R = 0.892808 and T = 0.046589 (hole). E_dielectric_square and E_metal_rectangle: the model of golden_gyptis_shapes_field with the shape replaced by a rectangle, exact direct solves, residuals 1.5e-12 and 2.2e-12 (square), 1.4e-12 and 6.1e-13 (rectangle); R = 0.036622 and T = 0.962998 (square), R = 0.640434 and T = 0.303694 (rectangle). The stored phasors are in gyptis's time convention, the conjugate of Wavebit's; the consumer maps them as -exp(2 pi i h / wavelength) * conj(E), with h the layer thickness
references.discretization: tetrahedral meshes graded toward the walls and their edges: 44075 cells for the block and for the hole (smallest edge 0.79 nm), 21544 cells for the dielectric square (4.78 nm) and 21453 for the metal rectangle (4.84 nm); the product side is a Fourier truncation of the same cell

generator.command: python fem_shape.py sq_T1 sq T1 12.25 1 for E_dielectric_square and python fem_shape.py rtmetal_T1 rt T1 -20-1.5j 1 for E_metal_rectangle (the script whose digest is given); the block model, another script of the same repository (sha256 45b1006cc1b578e1228beae7c5cac3a1e81203749b6c7bd1fa974129836d1b21), at its level T2 for E_metal_block and, with the two permittivities exchanged, for E_hole; then the plane samples laid out on the 48 x 48 grid

cost.note: four runs of two solves each, factorization out of core; the block and the hole took about 20 to 30 minutes each, the square and the rectangle about 5

shapes.E_metal_block: a 200 nm square of permittivity -20+1.5j (Wavebit convention) at the cell centre, in air
shapes.E_hole: a 200 nm square hole of air at the cell centre in a film of permittivity -20+1.5j
shapes.E_dielectric_square: a 200 nm square of permittivity 12.25 at the cell centre, in air
shapes.E_metal_rectangle: a rectangle 250 nm along x and 150 nm along y, permittivity -20+1.5j, at the cell centre, in air

samples.plane: mid-height of the layer, z = 75 nm above its lower face
samples.layout: each field as E[j, i, component] at (x[i], y[j]), components (Ex, Ey, Ez)

inputs.mesh_level: the block model's T2 for E_metal_block and E_hole (its T1 is the self-check); the shape model's T1 for the other two, which have no second level

outcomes.reference_self_check: over the same 2304 samples the block model's coarser level (22727 cells) differs from the stored one by 0.37% of the plane RMS of the in-plane field for the block (R 0.355677 against 0.356150) and by 0.20% for the hole (R 0.892590 against 0.892808). The dielectric square and the metal rectangle have one mesh level; the same script on the dielectric square reproduces the block model of that square in R (0.03662 against 0.03667). With the solve in stretched coordinates the square and the rectangle stop improving at 0.4% and 3.4% of the plane RMS from order 12 on, with the solve's R settled to five digits and 0.3% from the reference's, which is taken as these two references' own accuracy
